**Finding: compliant (sits at the fallback).**

Paragraph 22 of the APCN 2 Agreement satisfies every fallback element for ASSIGN, and it does so symmetrically — it binds all Parties, so nothing in it operates one-sidedly against Teleglobe USA:

- **Successor assignment (both parties):** 22.3(a)–(d) allow any Party to transfer the whole of its rights and obligations to a successor, Parent Company, Subsidiary or Affiliate **without any consent** — this actually reaches the preferred affiliate/successor carve-out.
- **Written notice:** 22.6 requires only timely written notice to the other Parties.
- **Other assignments require consent, not unreasonably withheld:** 22.1/22.2 route all other whole transfers through Management Committee consent, which "must not unreasonably withhold or delay its approval."
- **No change-of-control exposure:** searches for "change of control", "control", "ownership", "merger" returned nothing — there is no counterparty termination or re-pricing right triggered by a change of control of our party, so the walk-away scenarios are absent. Paragraph 30 binds successors and permitted assigns.

Noted in the rationale but **not redlined** (short of preferred wording only, not a fallback failure): partial affiliate assignments under 22.4 are allowed once per Assignee and do not release the Assignor; territorial assignments under 22.5 carry ownership/cost conditions; and there is no express bar on a counterparty assigning to our competitor — a limited concern in a multilateral consortium cable agreement.

No redline proposed, consistent with the instruction not to upgrade a fallback-compliant bargain to preferred wording.
